newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to invest $160 mln in northern provinces.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to invest $160 mln in northern provinces.

text.p: Morocco plans to invest $160 million in 1997/98 to upgrade infrastructure in northern provinces to eradicate drug trafficking and halt clandestine immigration to Europe, the official MAP news agency said.

Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali, who held a meeting with the region representatives in the eastern city of Oujda, was quoted by MAP as saying: "Morocco should count on its own means to finance the development in northern provinces...For the fiscal year 1997/98, it plans to invest 1.5 billion dirhams ($160 million) in the region."
Filali said, the government's long term plan called "the long-lasting integrated development programme for the northern provinces", requires a total investment of 15.4 billion dirhams.
Moroccan authorities were holding talks with the European Union and other Western countries to financially contribute to the development of the area, MAP said.

Morocco has already set up a management fund called "The Agency for Promotion and Development of Northern Provinces", to which the state budget will devote 300 million dirhams for the 1997/98 fiscal year, MAP added.
The authorities long term strategy aims to substitute cannabis cultivation with fruit and other crops to improve the country's image abroad and attract foreign investments to the region.
The targeted region includes provinces of Tangier, Tetouan, Chefchaouen, Larache, Al-Hoceima, Nador, Taounate, Taza and Oujda.
